clue.text: Strength available to take wooden vessel round river

parts.note: fir is a wood, so 'wooden' stands for the timber tree

indicators.note: the vessel goes round, enclosing the river's name

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Someone takes a wooden boat around a river, showing what strength they have to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the jug around Italy's river to give EPOWER. 'vessel' first suggests a boat, but here it is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: Firepower is the destructive strength a force has at its disposal, hence strength available.

clue.text: Step this way to pay little money, attending hospital

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay it
p is a penny, the smallest British coin
at means present at, attending

explanation.surface: An invitation to step this way to pay a small sum while at the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A path for pedestrians is literally where you step, so the phrase describes a walkway.

clue.text: World is sure heading for meltdown

parts.note: real and sure both mean genuine, certain

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gloomy prediction that the world is surely heading for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' picks the first letter of meltdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or world, as in the realm of science.

clue.text: Parisian parent about to split should send give it another try

indicators.note: the French father goes about, enclosing the word for splitting

parts.note: pere is French for father
to sever is to split apart

explanation.surface: A French father on the point of leaving is urged to give the relationship another go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the French father around the verb. 'should send' is in the clue as held but supplies no letters, probably an OCR slip.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep trying despite setbacks, so to have another go.

clue.text: Legless killer in desire to be irascible CA

indicators.note: the snake sits in the word for desire

parts.note: a wish is a desire
an asp is a venomous snake, a killer without legs

explanation.surface: A snake inside someone's longing makes them bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the snake inside the longing. The stray 'CA' in the held clue is an OCR fragment that plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish means sharply irritable, as quick to sting as a wasp, so irascible.

clue.text: Talk of private resentment

indicators.note: spoken talk signals that a word is said, not spelt

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, such as a private

explanation.surface: Gossip about someone's private grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk of' says RANKER is heard, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep bitter resentment, a long-held grudge.

clue.text: Locator of plane travelling there and back

indicators.note: the word reads the same going out and coming back, signalling a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Tracking an aircraft on its return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar systems detect and locate aircraft, so it finds a plane.

clue.text: Go through Exeter if leaving centre

indicators.note: the letters are taken from the middle of this run of words

explanation.surface: Someone passing through Exeter, if they are leaving the city centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' picks letters from inside 'Exeter if leaving'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through something is to search it hastily, going through its contents.

clue.text: Ruthless old magistrate got DA replaced

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of old Venice and Genoa

indicators.note: the letters are placed anew in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old official got the district attorney replaced in a cut-throat move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges GOTDA to ATDOG. DA looks like a district attorney but is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-eat-dog world is one of ruthless competition, the phrase used as an adjective.

clue.text: Shoot athlete

definitions.meaning: a creeping stem sent out by a plant such as a strawberry
a ... competes in races on foot

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a stem a plant sends out and a sprinter or distance competitor.

clue.text: 21% of this + 78% of that makes this, now showing

parts.note: air is about 21 per cent oxygen, chemical symbol O
air is about 78 per cent nitrogen, chemical symbol N
this refers throughout to the gas we breathe

explanation.surface: A puzzling bit of arithmetic about mixing proportions, presented as a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Every 'this' and 'that' is the atmosphere: its oxygen and nitrogen shares give O and N, and together they make it.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is being broadcast, now showing to viewers.

clue.text: Jocular issue of Browning, perhaps?

parts.note: Browning looks like the poet, but it is a make of firearm; the offspring of a firearm is a playful exclamation of mild exasperation

explanation.surface: A joke about the child of the poet Robert Browning.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning seems to be the poet; it is the firearm maker, so his issue is a firearm's child.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular, mildly affectionate term for a rascal, literally the child of a firearm.

clue.text: With ceremony that is making comeback, I preserved city

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial display

indicators.note: coming back means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: ie abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A ceremonious return for a once-buried city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' turns IE into EI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was buried and so preserved by the ash of Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Without Conservative, manage to consider act

indicators.note: without means the abbreviation is dropped from the word for manage

parts.note: to cope is to manage
to rate something is to consider or reckon it

explanation.surface: A politician without the Tories tries to manage while weighing how to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes C from COPE, leaving OPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or act, as a machine operates.

clue.text: Next number wins for nation

parts.note: then means next, afterwards
ether is an anaesthetic, something that numbs: a number
to land something is to win it, as in land a contract

explanation.surface: The next number drawn wins for one country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that makes you numb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Netherlands is a European country, so a nation.

clue.text: Please record money head of authority's invested

parts.note: to enter details is to record them

indicators.note: the letter is put inside, invested in, the word for money

parts.note: tin is slang for money

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A request to record that money has been invested by the head of an authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' takes A from authority's and 'invested' puts it in TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain is to amuse or please people.

clue.text: Police work is remarkable

definitions.meaning: ... suspects is a basic part of police work

explanation.definitionFit: Both readings fit: the act of detaining a suspect and the adjective for eye-catching.

clue.text: One banned from touchline for changing strip

indicators.note: changing means the remaining letters are put into a new order
the letter is excluded from the word, as a player is banned from the field

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A footballer is sent off the touchline for changing his strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banned from' takes I out of touchline, leaving TOUCHLNE, which 'changing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclothe someone is to undress or strip them.

clue.text: The king put in danger upon failing legendary monarch

indicators.note: the first pieces are put inside the rearranged letters
failing means the letters collapse into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
R abbreviates rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is placed in peril because something he relied on failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges DANGERUPON to UPENDRAGON and 'put in' puts THER after its U.
explanation.definitionFit: Uther Pendragon is the legendary British king, father of Arthur.

clue.text: Black and white dish with nothing on top

parts.note: a pie is a dish
bald means with no hair on top of the head

explanation.surface: A monochrome dish with no topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Piebald describes an animal patched in black and white.

clue.text: Puzzle seen only negatively?

definitions.meaning: to puzzle someone is to baffle them
read as ..., the phrase means not a plus, something regarded only as a negative

explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to perplex them so they do not know how to respond.

clue.text: Weightlifter's pole needs shortening for swimmer

indicators.note: shortening means the last letter is cut off the phrase's word

parts.note: a barbell is the bar a weightlifter lifts

explanation.surface: A weightlifter's bar needs cutting down to suit a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs shortening' trims the last L off BARBELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbel is a freshwater fish, a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: A connection is cut

parts.note: a bridge is a connection between two places

explanation.surface: A link between two places has been severed.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or cut it.

clue.text: Look to knock down ---- out cold knockout!

indicators.note: out means the letter for cold is removed

parts.note: to deck someone is to knock them down
C abbreviates cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A boxer is told to see the opponent knocked down and out cold for a knockout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes C from DECK, leaving DEK.
explanation.definitionFit: Dekko is British slang for a look, as in have a dekko.

clue.text: Snort compound, single line - - through here?

indicators.note: a compound is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: one, a single, is I

explanation.surface: Snorting a drug compound, a single line, through the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' rearranges SNORTI to NOSTRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of powder is snorted up through the opening of the nose.

clue.text: Black man believing in rise of an emperor

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: a tsar was the emperor of Russia

explanation.surface: A believer in the resurrection of an emperor, Haile Selassie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' turns ATSAR upwards to read RASTA. Rastafarians revere Ethiopia's emperor Haile Selassie.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian follows a faith founded among Black Jamaicans, a believer.

clue.text: What's last to be pocketed in bar?

definitions.meaning: in snooker the ... is the last one potted
to bar them from a club

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the final snooker ball potted and a vote to exclude someone.

clue.text: Popular group's lesser feature

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A popular band's minor attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small subsidiary picture or map within a larger one.

clue.text: Tempo fast approaching zero

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
O resembles zero

explanation.surface: A speed approaching nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is a slow tempo marking in music.

clue.text: Appoint European to make mark during meeting

indicators.note: during puts these pieces inside the word for meeting

parts.note: a date is a meeting
to sign is to make one's mark

explanation.surface: A European is appointed to sign during a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts ESIGN inside DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To designate someone is to appoint them to a post.
